substantial.problem: AP9 is drafted on Saw Solomon Opehtoo's MA thesis (Episcopal Divinity School, 2014) as the 'one modern study' G89-31 (a) and Slices (AS2) require before drafting ('if none can be confirmed, hold it'). The thesis does not meet that bar. (1) It is an unpublished student thesis, not a peer-reviewed study. (2) It is a work of constructive theology ('In Search of Karen Theology'), and its history chapter rests on the same missionary sources the study was meant to check: Mason 1843 and Harris 1920 (its footnotes 33-36). It gives no independent check of Mason. (3) It is not cited by the record and is not public domain (archive.org: CC BY-NC-ND 3.0; the file says 'Copyright by Saw Solomon Opehtoo 2014'), so it falls outside the Drafting Brief's rule for added sources. (4) The sentence 'It did not always stay a liberating force' is the author's undated judgment. In the thesis it leads straight into 'Current Theologies of Christian Karens', a critique of present-day (post-2006) Karen Baptist teaching. So it brings a present-day verdict into an era 9 row. (5) 'A writer trained at a Karen Baptist seminary tells of...' is an anonymous framing that reads as filler.

notes:
Independent check: I re-fetched all nine raw texts in AS2/raw/SOURCES.json with curl into review/AS2/raw/. All nine are byte-identical to the drafter's copies, which are therefore unaltered archive.org djvu text. No raw file is HTML. I ran check_draft.py against my own fetch: 159 quotes, 0 QUOTE-MISS, 0 RAW-MISSING. The only output is two READ-FAIL lines, both for paragraph [0] of VII.2 (FRE 30) and VIII.27 (FRE 27). I confirmed against the census that both paragraphs are identical to the frozen text (the census longDescription is a prefix of the new value, and it is one paragraph). They are not the drafter's to fix. The Library quote (Collectanea, 25 August 1675) was read at its lines. I read about 40 quotes in context, beyond the verbatim match, to check that the sentences they carry are supported. Those reads produced S2-S7 and M1-M8. Nothing is invented: no blocking finding.

Questions put to this review:
(1) AP9 on an MA thesis: it does not meet 'one modern study' (S1). Hold AP9, as Slices says to when no study can be confirmed.
(2) Aritonang and Dutton: the sweep record cites both as V, opened raw. The Drafting Brief's public-domain condition applies only to sources the record does not cite. So sentences may rest on them, and link quotes from them are 'verified-online', capped at Widely Accepted. That cap is the right ceiling for their uncontested statements. Where one of them conflicts with another source (Dutton's 1660 against Launay's 1658, S4), the prose names both sides. Short attributed quotes are the census's normal practice. Record the licenses (M12). Opehtoo, by contrast, is neither record-cited nor public domain.
(3) The Society of Jesus (VI.11) → vietnamese-catholicism-to-1815, 'gave rise to', Widely Accepted: the type matches census precedent (VI.11 → kirishitan-japan, → china-mission-born-christianity, → philippine-catholicism), and the grade fits a raw modern study. The 1620s sit inside VI.11's 1540-1650 window. Approve, with the note fixed (S3).
(4) VOC → indonesian-christianity 'influenced': mis-typed (S7).
(5) VOC → catholics-of-dutch-ceylon, 'argued against', Dominant Modern Reconstruction, major by outcome: approve. 'Argued against' is the census's type for a hostile institutional act (catholic-church-ancien-regime → the-society-of-jesus for the 1773 suppression). The outcome rests on an institutional act shown in the link's own quote (Chitty's report of the plakaat of 19 September 1658). The act was the Company government's, and the outcome's 'A Dutch proclamation' says so honestly. Dominant Modern Reconstruction is conservative but defensible, since the force/no-force dispute is named in the note.
(6) The 1658 vs 1660 conflict: S4.
(7) VII.2's dates kept at 1675-1750 while the line reaches 1813: faithful to the ruling. Flag it to Mark (M11).
(8) Living: no carrier exists in the census. living:false is still wrong under P2-V (S8), and the fix belongs to the coordinator's living pass.
(9) MEP named in AP4 (G89-2 a): done in segment 1 ('A new Paris mission society, the MEP, was set up to send them priests'). Name it in segment 2 as well (M3). There is no MEP row and no MEP link, which is correct under G89-2 (a).

Ruling fidelity otherwise holds. AP4 enters in two segments, split at 1815 (G89-25 b). AP5 enters as an era 8 row (G89-27 a). AP6 enters as a Ceylon row, 1658-1806 (G89-28 a). AP8 enters as a line in VII.2 (G89-32 a). AP10 (G89-33 b), AP12 (G89-35 c) and AP13 (G89-30 c) are held, and AP14 is listed as carried (G89-37 a). VII.2 and VIII.27 are changed only in longDescription, voices and sources (the old lists are kept whole). VIII.26 and VIII.39 are untouched. The era rules hold: nothing after 1815 appears in the era 8 rows. The one exception is S1's 'liberating force' sentence, which brings in a present-day judgment.

Counts: 0 blocking, 8 substantial, 13 minor. Verdict: revise. Round 2 can be a targeted recheck of S1-S8 and M1-M13 only.
